description: Three to five short spoken lines an hour about the ground a route is on: one sentence, at the point the driver reaches the thing it is about, and then silence. Not a tour and not a chatbot. NOTHING IS GENERATED HERE: every line is a sentence a person wrote from a public-domain plaque inscription and a person reviewed, compiled into the gateway binary, so no model runs in this path and the lines are identical for every driver. Give `geometry_polyline6` from the `route` tool and, IMPORTANT, `duration_s` from the same answer: without it the silence budget falls back to a distance, and "four lines an hour" is a claim about time that a distance answers wrongly at both ends. Optional `min_gap_s`, `min_gap_m`, `max_offset_m` (default 60, hard ceiling 80), `max_lines` and `voice_format` ("opus" or "m4a", which adds each line's audio cache key and URL and NEVER synthesises). COVERAGE IS ONE CORRIDOR, deliberately: the Chelsea riverside, 18 reviewed lines over 5 km. EVERY OTHER ROUTE ANSWERS WITH NO LINES, and that is a correct answer rather than a failure. ALWAYS READ THE CENSUS, which is the record of WHAT WAS NOT SAID: no lines with every entry in `beyond_reach` means this feature does not cover the journey; no lines with entries in `silenced_by_budget` means the corridor is covered and the budget is holding them back. They are different answers and must never be relayed the same way. On the reference route the census reports 1 spoken and 17 silenced, which is the design working, not a thin corpus. Every line publishes `offset_m`, the measured distance from the plaque to the route, because it is the entire warrant for the word "here", and `plaque_ids` so any claim can be taken back to its source. TWO OMISSIONS ARE DELIBERATE: no line says anything is visible, still standing or unchanged (a plaque records that somebody was somewhere, and nothing more), and NO LINE SAYS WHICH SIDE OF THE ROAD anything is on, because nothing in the source records it and a look that finds nothing spends the driver's trust in everything else. Do not add either. COSTS 1 UNIT a call: it reads no tiles and opens no archive. Requires the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY).

duration_s.description:
That route's own duration, seconds: `duration_s` from the same
answer. **Supply it.** Without it the silence budget falls back to
a distance, and "three to five lines an hour" is a claim about
time that a distance answers wrongly at both ends.

geometry_polyline6.description:
The route shape, precision-6 encoded: `geometry_polyline6`
straight out of the `route` tool's answer.

max_lines.description: Ceiling on how many lines come back, 1 to 50 (default 12).

max_offset_m.description:
How near a plaque must come to the route before its line may be
spoken, metres (default 60, hard ceiling 80).

min_gap_m.description:
Least distance between two lines, metres (default 400). A floor
under the time budget in every case.

min_gap_s.description:
Least time between two lines, seconds (default 900, which is four
an hour). Applied only with `duration_s`.

voice_format.description:
Container to address each line's audio clip in: `opus` or `m4a`.
Given, every line gains a `clip` with its synthesis cache key and
URL. It NEVER synthesises: the key is a pure function of the
sentence, so asking here buys nothing.

name: heritage_narration

HeritageLine.description: One reviewed line about the ground the route is on.

at_m.description: Distance along the route where this belongs, metres.

basis.description: What the line rests on, in words.

clip.description:
The line's audio address (only when `voice_format` was given):
`hash`, `url` and `format`. Nothing was synthesised to produce it.

id.description:
The corpus entry's own id, stable across responses, so a client
can remember which lines it has already played.

offset_m.description:
Measured perpendicular distance from the plaque's own recorded
coordinate to the route, metres. Published on every line because
it is the entire warrant for the word "here", and because the
coordinate behind it was recorded by a volunteer and has never
been surveyed.

plaque_ids.description:
The source plaque records, by their OpenPlaques id, so any claim
can be taken back to its source.

say.description:
The sentence to say, verbatim. Written by a person from a
public-domain plaque inscription and reviewed by a person.

subject.description: The subject's name as the source dataset records it.

attribution.description: The licence notice for this answer.

caveat.description: The standing limits, for relaying to users.

census.description:
The census of what was NOT said: `corpus_entries`, `within_reach`,
`beyond_reach`, `spoken`, `silenced_by_budget`, the gap that was
applied and what it was derived from. An empty `lines` with every
entry in `beyond_reach` means this feature does not cover the
journey; an empty `lines` with entries in `silenced_by_budget`
means the budget is working. They are different answers and must
not be reported the same way.

corridor.description:
The corridor that was consulted: its id, name, the road it runs
on and the date its lines were reviewed.

lines.description:
The lines, in route order. Empty is the ordinary answer nearly
everywhere: read `census` before saying anything about it.
